study_info.title: Effects of Ergocalciferol Added to Calcium on the Risk of Falls in Elderly High-Risk Women
study_info.authors: Richard L. Prince, MD; Nicole Austin, BSc; Amanda Devine, PhD; Ian M. Dick, PhD; David Bruce, MD; Kun Zhu, PhD
study_info.study_design: Population-based, double-blind, randomized controlled trial. Randomization was performed using a random number generator with a block size of 10 by an independent research scientist.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Women aged 70 to 90 years, community-dwelling, ambulant, living in Perth, Australia, with a history of falling in the past 12 months and a plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration of less than 24.0 ng/mL.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Current vitamin D consumption; current consumption of bone or mineral active agents apart from calcium; a bone mineral density z score at the total hip site of less than −2.0; medical conditions or disorders that influence bone mineral metabolism, including laboratory evidence of renal insufficiency (a creatinine level more than 2-fold above the reference range); a fracture in the past 6 months; a Mini-Mental State Examination score of less than 24; or the presence of marked neurological conditions likely to substantially impair balance or physical activity, such as stroke and Parkinson disease.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Patients attending the emergency departments of teaching hospitals, patients receiving services from the local community home nursing service for management of falls, and the electoral roll that lists more than 98% of women of this age range.

minimal_units.intervention_details: Ergocalciferol 1000 IU/d (Ostelin; Boots Healthcare, North Ryde, Australia) consumed with the evening meal for 1 year, plus calcium citrate 1000 mg/d (Citracal; Mission Pharmacal, Key Pharmaceutical Pty Ltd, Rhodes, Australia) as two 250-mg tablets in the morning with breakfast and two 250-mg tablets with the evening meal.

outcomes.comparison_targets: Ergocalciferol with Calcium Citrate vs Placebo with Calcium Citrate

minimal_units.control_details: Placebo (Ostelin; Boots Healthcare, North Ryde, Australia) consumed with the evening meal for 1 year, plus calcium citrate 1000 mg/d (Citracal; Mission Pharmacal, Key Pharmaceutical Pty Ltd, Rhodes, Australia) as two 250-mg tablets in the morning with breakfast and two 250-mg tablets with the evening meal.

outcomes.comparison_targets: Ergocalciferol with Calcium Citrate vs Placebo with Calcium Citrate

meta_analysis_parameters.outcome_domain: major adverse cardiovascular events；myocardial infarction；stroke or cerebrovascular events；cardiovascular disease mortality；all-cause mortality
